name: Operator console
builtFor: Console operators at Site Alpha and Site Bravo, and air-defence commanders in the central ops room
summary: A prototype console that puts the radar track, RF contact and camera for one drone in a single view. It lets operators escalate with the evidence attached, and lets commanders acknowledge and record a decision from one panel.

whyWeBuiltThis: Operators at Sites Alpha and Bravo confirm a drone across radar, RF and camera tools that share no identity or clock for a target. They match tracks to emitters by eye and point the camera by hand.
Operators escalate by voice with no sign that the commander has it. Commanders spend 20 to 40 seconds a call getting the operator's picture.
Afterwards, it is hard to show who confirmed and authorised what, and a review takes a few days. All of this sits inside about 90 seconds to decide once a drone is confirmed.
overview.whatWeEnvision: Operators confirm a drone from one view, without matching tracks and emitters by eye. Commanders get the evidence in front of them and authorise without a voice description. Operators can see that an escalation has been received. Every step is recorded as it happens. Every engagement decision stays with a human.

whereWeAreAt.blurb: The console is a prototype and has not been tested with users. These figures show how the work was done before the console, taken from field notes. They are not results for the console.

features.title: One view per target
features.body: Shows the radar track, the RF contact and the camera together under one target identifier, and states whether radar and RF were matched. The track is marked on the camera picture, and the camera can be pointed from the target.

features.title: Source status and age
features.body: Shows whether each of the three feeds is live, stale or dropped, and how old its last data is.

features.title: Escalation and acknowledgement
features.body: The operator escalates in one action with the evidence attached. The commander acknowledges with one action that the operator can see, and records a decision from the evidence panel.

features.title: Decision record
features.body: Records each confirmation, escalation, acknowledgement and authorisation as it happens, with the sources, the people and the times.

features.title: Two sites, one console
features.body: Lists both sites together, and shows an alert from the other site as it arrives. The evidence for this is one interview.

notes.text:
The product requirements for Operator-console-v1 cover nine user stories across five modules. Handover and the alert flood are out of scope for v1.
A usability test is planned with six console operators and two air-defence commanders. No results are filed yet.

next: Run the usability test and file the results.
Run the System Usability Scale and the satisfaction question with the same participants.
